A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visual-information-processing study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison; v2 retains the original appendices and adds two.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-ablation experiments, logit-lens case studies, and attention-blocking results in Sections 3-4, Tables 1-2, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds quantitative object-token correspondence analyses and LLaVA-Phi-3 attention-blocking results, including Figures 6-8.

M1.justification: Mean-token ablation, logit-lens decoding, and attention knockout retain their underlying procedures. The added model evaluations, correspondence measurements, and layer-window scans extend the experimental analysis without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Coverage remains natural-image object identification through descriptions, binary polling, curated VQA, and visual-token analysis. The added COCO-validation subsets quantify existing phenomena; their splits, sample selection, and model configurations change evaluation settings rather than introduce a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same object, buffered-object, register-token, Integrated Gradients, and random-ablation comparisons. Qwen2VL is an additional model being analyzed, not a new comparison method evaluated against the interpretability procedure.

E3.justification: v2 adds quantitative correspondence protocols: 170 COCO-validation images with 20,000-30,000-pixel objects for LLaVA, 253 validation images for Qwen2VL-2B, and best-layer correspondence summaries. It also adds sliding 10-layer attention-blocking windows for LLaVA-Phi-3. The original LLaVA fixed-window experiment remains intact.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 supplements qualitative examples with aggregate layerwise correspondence analysis and a generalization check outside the LLaVA family. Section 4.2 adds a finer-grained Phi-3 replication testing where object information transfers and whether the last visual row acts as a summary. These substantially expand support for two central findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added correspondence and attention-blocking curves provide point estimates and averages without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 are numerically identical. New results include reported average best-layer correspondence of 23.7% for LLaVA and 6.5% for Qwen2VL, with best-layer locations summarized as 25.7/33 and 25.1/29. Figure 8 adds Phi-3 results showing stronger middle-to-late object-token blocking effects and minimal last-visual-row effects. These are additional findings under new analysis settings.

T1.justification: The transformer equations, embedding notation, mean-ablation definition, and attention-mask intervention remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain their claims. The conclusion modestly qualifies the attention-flow claim: experiments previously 'showed' direct extraction, whereas v2 says they 'suggest' VLMs 'may extract' object information.

C2.justification: v2 adds a tentative adapter-based explanation for Qwen's early-layer correspondence and interprets the shared refinement pattern as potentially general across adapter-style VLMs. It also explains the norm-preservation rationale for mean ablation. The architecture and complex-task limitations largely survive in condensed form.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that generative descriptions are checked for verbatim object-name occurrence and that Figure 3 combines labels from multiple middle-to-late layers. It documents sampling and window settings for the new analyses. Code, model-source, and demonstration links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen2-VL reference and a 'Parallel Work' paragraph crediting Jiang et al. (2025) and Wu et al. (2024) with related logit-lens findings and applications. Existing citations and the main positioning relative to attribution and mechanistic-interpretability research are retained.

P1.justification: Related work, the global-feature discussion, and the conclusion are condensed; limitations and future work are combined. There are localized explanations, typo corrections, and author/header edits, while the principal section order and most methodological prose remain stable.

P2.justification: New Appendices C-D introduce two layerwise correspondence plots and a six-panel attention-blocking figure, substantially expanding the graphical evidence. Original Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-2 are retained, with limited caption clarifications and conference-format layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the previously qualitative logit-lens evidence through quantitative analysis and a Qwen2VL check, while the Phi-3 replication supports the attention-flow interpretation. These provide a clear gain in empirical grounding. Reporting remains imperfect: Figures 6-7 describe best-layer summaries as peaks while plotting layerwise averages, obscuring the distinction between the statistics. The overall improvement is useful but limited.
